notes: Verifier = a VLM that answers one checklist item at a time from 12 labelled images (6 views of the original and edited object); it does not see code.

Accuracy is item-level agreement with the human label on the 264-item set; maj@3 is the main metric for the 14 verifiers; GPT-5.6-sol medium pass@1 is the verifier actually used for the main results table (230/264 = 87.1%).
Astra − Sol (maj@3) paired difference +4.17 pp, 95% source-cluster bootstrap CI [+0.00, +7.55] (exp2 rescored REPORT): not a stable ranking.
Excluding the 26 uncertain-flagged items, GPT-5.6-sol medium is 91.6% (INVENTORY §5; not recomputed here).

Display names: verifier id "luna" = GPT-5.6-luna, "gpt6luna" = GPT-6-luna; editor "claude_opus" = Claude Opus 4.8, "claude_sonnet" = Claude Sonnet 4.6, "claude_haiku" = Claude Haiku 4.5 (per main_performance/summary.csv).
Six-view strips: 6 tiles of 168x168 in order front, back, left, right, top, bottom. Original and edited share one bounding box per case, so relative size is meaningful.
explanation fields are short harvest descriptions of what the renders show; annotators recorded no rationales. v160_rationale is the Codex reviewer's verbatim text.
gaps: Spatial relations & connectivity and part–attribute grounding have no human-labelled example: none of the 34 Sol-medium errors on the human set clearly fit them, so v160 (Codex-reviewed) examples are used.
Category assignment for human-labelled examples is done in this harvest (provisional), pending the planned human coding of the 34 errors.
Metric-geometry labels are threshold judgments; the two metric examples are honest but debatable cases.
Several human labels used here were changed by the 2026-09-17 patch (yes→no); flagged per example.

human_set.design: 11 editor models x 6 levels x 4 items = 264 checklist items (44 per level, 24 per editor), balanced per cell — not proportional to the benchmark distribution
human_set.patch_changes: 11 labels changed vs original (10 yes→no, 1 no→yes)
human_set.policy: All 264 items included regardless of uncertainty flags; item-level accuracy; primary maj@3, predetermined trial1 supplementary.
human_set.annotation_conditions: Assisted adjudication, not blinded: the labelling UI showed the full query and the three GPT-5.6-sol high-effort answers with evidence (audit README). Single shared annotator workspace; no inter-annotator agreement study (README; INVENTORY).
human_set.images: 12 images per item (original + edited, 6 views each), same images the verifiers saw

rows.flag: 15th setting: historical GPT-5.6-sol high-effort votes (v158), shown to the annotator during labelling; not part of the 14-verifier comparison
single medium-effort call per item (pass@1); this is the verifier used for the main results table
2 items lack a complete 3-vote set in the final condition and are counted as wrong (exp2 rescored REPORT)

taxonomy.scheme: v160 data-backed capability taxonomy (visible_v160_verifier_taxonomy_20260831/REPORT.md). Categories were coded by Codex re-checking images in a stratified audit of Sol medium-vs-high disagreements; there is no taxonomy coded against human labels yet (INVENTORY §5).
taxonomy.share_source: statistics.json weighted_error_counts_within_disagreements: weighted error composition within the 1,225 six-view medium-vs-high disagreements (audit n=242, 235 decisive) from the v158 run (17,188 items). Not a share of all verifier errors.
taxonomy.example_policy: Examples marked label_source=human_patch_20260917 come from the 34 GPT-5.6-sol medium errors on the 264-item human set; their category is assigned in this harvest unless stated. Examples marked v160_codex_review take both label and category from the v160 audit (not human).

categories.name: Comparative / metric geometry
categories.definition: Estimating ratios, thickness, spacing, angles or a "conspicuous" change, calibrated between the original and edited images.

examples.instruction: Keep the underlying original object category broadly recognizable while applying the requested semantic reinterpretation; Reconstruct the ascending tread stack as a spiral of broad overlapping leaf-shaped steps with clearly pointed outer tips; reshape the central support into a thick irregular tree trunk with strongly flared contours; replace the round base with a wide cluster of raised spreading roots; rebuild several exposed supports beneath the stair turns as thick forked branches reaching from the trunk; reshape the top landing into a large leafy canopy platform with a scalloped perimeter
examples.checklist_item: Are several stair turns supported by thick forked branches reaching from the trunk?
examples.verifier_evidence: Compared with the original’s unsupported spiral turns around a plain column, the modified right view visibly shows multiple thick brown branching braces extending from the trunk beneath several projecting green stair turns.
examples.label_source: human_patch_20260917 (main_patch_20260917T012508Z) — label changed in the patch: yes→no
examples.category_source: v160_codex_review primary_capability (comparative_metric_geometry) — this item is in both the human set and the v160 audit, and both say "no"
examples.explanation: Thickness threshold: the right view shows only thin brown twigs under a few leaf-shaped steps; Sol medium described them as "thick brown branching braces" and passed the item.
examples.explanation_source: harvest observation of the renders (annotator recorded no rationale)
examples.v160_rationale: The leaf-shaped steps attach directly around the straight trunk; several thick forked branch supports beneath exposed turns are not visible.

examples.instruction: Keep the modified result identifiable and visually coherent as a version of the source object while applying the requested edits; Reconstruct the cabinet with a large square central opening surrounded on all four sides by a continuous ring of smaller compartments; make the central opening span roughly half the cabinet width and half its length; divide each long side of the surrounding ring into three equal openings; divide each short side of the surrounding ring into two equal openings; raise the central opening's perimeter walls conspicuously above the outer compartment walls
examples.checklist_item: Does the central opening span roughly half the cabinet width and half its length?
examples.verifier_evidence: In the modified bottom view, the clear central opening is visibly only about one-third of the cabinet width and roughly two-fifths of its length, rather than approximately half in both dimensions.
examples.category_source: assigned in this harvest from the v160 definitions (provisional; not human-coded)
examples.explanation: Which boundary to measure: in the bottom view the clear hole is roughly 0.35–0.4 of the cabinet width (harvest pixel estimate), close to Sol's "one-third", while the raised central well including its walls spans roughly 0.6; the annotator accepted "roughly half", Sol rejected.
examples.explanation_source: harvest observation of the renders (annotator recorded no rationale)

categories.name: Spatial relations & connectivity
categories.definition: Judging support, contact, attachment, load-bearing, orientation, relative position and cross-part relations.

examples.instruction: Keep the modified result identifiable and visually coherent as a version of the source object while applying the requested edits; Reconstruct the bracket as a split-level frame with a high rear bridge, two low side rails, and a raised front bridge; connect the high rear bridge to both low side rails with long sloping transition ramps; connect the low side rails to the raised front bridge with two short vertical steps; open a broad centered archway through the raised front bridge; cut one large elongated opening along each low side rail between the rear ramps and front steps
examples.checklist_item: Do two short vertical steps connect the low side rails to the raised front bridge?
examples.verifier_evidence: In the modified front view, the raised horizontal front bridge is visibly joined down to the low rails by two short vertical end risers, one on each side of the broad centered opening; these split-level connections are absent in the original.
examples.label_source: v160_codex_review (image re-check by Codex in the v160 taxonomy audit; NOT a human label)
examples.v160_rationale: The modified result collapses visually to a single long plate in every view, with neither low side rails nor two short vertical connectors to a raised bridge.
examples.explanation: The edited part is a single long plate in the front view; there are no separate low rails or risers, yet Sol described "two short vertical end risers" joining a raised bridge.
examples.explanation_source: harvest summary of the v160 rationale + render check

examples.instruction: Keep the original source object visibly present and broadly recognizable within the completed scene; Fix the upright extrusion to a broad vibration-test base with a thick platform and four large isolator feet; add a linear actuator with a long cylindrical body and piston rod pressing against the extrusion's side; add a dial indicator with a large round gauge and articulated mounting arm touching the opposite side of the extrusion; add a tall test console with a wide control panel and substantial cabinet base beside the platform; build an open test rig with two tall columns and a crossbeam anchored to the base, supporting the actuator and dial-indicator arm while adjoining the console
examples.checklist_item: Is the upright extrusion fixed to a broad vibration-test base with a thick platform and four large isolator feet?
examples.verifier_evidence: The modified front view shows a broad thick platform, but the yellow upright extrusion visibly ends above it with a clear gap, so it is not fixed to the base.
examples.label_source: v160_codex_review (image re-check by Codex in the v160 taxonomy audit; NOT a human label)
examples.v160_rationale: A broad thick platform and four large isolator feet are unambiguous.
examples.explanation: The extrusion is mounted in a test rig on a thick platform with large feet (v160: "unambiguous"); Sol read a visible gap below the extrusion as "not fixed to the base" and failed the item.
examples.explanation_source: harvest summary of the v160 rationale + render check

categories.name: Identity & preservation
categories.definition: Separating allowed target edits from severe non-target damage, and deciding whether the object is still recognizable.

examples.instruction: Keep the modified result identifiable and visually coherent as a version of the source object while applying the requested edits; Rebuild the lower trunk and two opposing side arms as a broad arch-shaped crown supported by two tall outer uprights; curve the two outer uprights inward above the shortened central trunk so their tips nearly meet with a narrow gap; create one large rounded opening framed by the outer arms and positioned entirely above the central trunk tip; make the two outer uprights reach the same height and stand conspicuously taller than the central trunk; flare both arm-to-trunk transitions into broad sweeping curves that widen the lower half of the arch
examples.checklist_item: Is the modified result still an identifiable and visually coherent version of the source object, without severe corruption of parts not targeted by the requested edits?
examples.verifier_evidence: The modified front view remains a coherent cactus-like form with a central trunk, two symmetrical outer arms, rounded organic surfaces, and retained spine details; the substantial silhouette changes correspond to the targeted rebuild, with no visible severe corruption of non-targeted parts.
examples.category_source: assigned in this harvest from the v160 definitions (provisional; not human-coded); exp3 casebook tagged it preservation_scope_ambiguity (whether preservation applies under a requested rebuild)
examples.explanation: The edited object is a ring-like loop on a short stem with no recognizable cactus trunk or arms; Sol called it "a coherent cactus-like form" and passed the preservation item.
examples.explanation_source: harvest observation of the renders (annotator recorded no rationale)

examples.instruction: Keep the modified result identifiable and visually coherent as a version of the source object while applying the requested edits; Lengthen both front claws so their pincer tips project much farther ahead of the carapace.
examples.checklist_item: Is the modified result still an identifiable and visually coherent version of the source object, without severe corruption of parts not targeted by the requested edits?
examples.verifier_evidence: The matched back view shows the carapace and all non-targeted walking legs remain intact and closely match the original, so the result is still clearly identifiable as the same crab despite the substantial claw edit.
examples.label_source: v160_codex_review (image re-check by Codex in the v160 taxonomy audit; NOT a human label)
examples.v160_rationale: Both elongated claw pincers float detached well ahead of their arm stubs, which is severe corruption.
examples.explanation: Both pincers float detached well ahead of their arm stubs (clear in the top view); Sol checked the back view, saw intact body and legs, and passed the preservation item.
examples.explanation_source: harvest summary of the v160 rationale + render check

categories.name: Fine-grained shape
categories.definition: Distinguishing neighbouring shape concepts such as V vs U, crescent vs fork, wedge vs plate, rounded vs sharp corners.

examples.instruction: Keep the underlying original object category broadly recognizable while applying the requested semantic reinterpretation; Reshape the carapace into a broad low Art Deco teardrop with three clearly separated stepped perimeter tiers; rebuild both claws as long streamlined crescent pincers with wide open tips; rebuild the walking legs as repeated angular double-zigzag struts ending in broad triangular fin feet; transform the two eye stalks into tall fan-shaped ornamental stalks; add three large geometric fins radiating from the rear rim
examples.checklist_item: Are the two eye stalks transformed into tall fan-shaped ornamental stalks?
examples.verifier_evidence: The original shows two short, narrow upright eye stalks, while the modified view shows two distinct tall, symmetric ornamental stalks with widened, angular fan-like structures.
examples.label_source: human_patch_20260917 (main_patch_20260917T012508Z) — label changed in the patch: yes→no
examples.category_source: assigned in this harvest from the v160 definitions (provisional; not human-coded)
examples.explanation: In the left view the eye stalks became clusters of thin diverging spikes on a frame; the (patched) human label rejects "tall fan-shaped ornamental stalks", Sol accepted.
examples.explanation_source: harvest observation of the renders (annotator recorded no rationale)

examples.instruction: Keep the underlying original object category broadly recognizable while applying the requested semantic reinterpretation; Reconstruct the ascending tread stack as a sleek futuristic spiral of broad trapezoidal platforms with alternating sharply chamfered outer ends; reshape the central support into a tall segmented rocket-like column that tapers toward the top; replace the circular base with a wide layered hexagonal launch-pad pedestal; add four large vertical stabilizer fins around the lower portion of the central column; rebuild the top landing as a thick ring-shaped docking platform with a clearly open center
examples.checklist_item: Is the ascending tread stack a sleek futuristic spiral of broad trapezoidal platforms with alternating sharply chamfered outer ends?
examples.verifier_evidence: Compared with the original right view’s narrow radial steps and smooth curved perimeter, the modified stack visibly forms a continuous futuristic spiral of broad trapezoidal platforms whose outer tips repeat a sharply angled, alternating chamfer pattern.
examples.label_source: v160_codex_review (image re-check by Codex in the v160 taxonomy audit; NOT a human label)
examples.v160_rationale: The modified stair is a narrow, irregular twisting stack; it lacks broad trapezoidal platforms with alternating sharply chamfered outer ends.
examples.explanation: The edited stair is a narrow, irregular twisting stack; Sol saw "broad trapezoidal platforms" with "alternating chamfer" tips.
examples.explanation_source: harvest summary of the v160 rationale + render check

categories.name: Topology & openings
categories.definition: Judging hollow vs solid, holes / slots / notches, open vs closed, through-passages and central voids.

examples.instruction: Keep the modified result identifiable and visually coherent as a version of the source object while applying the requested edits; Reconstruct the staircase as three broad straight flights stacked in an alternating switchback path; place the lowest flight on a wide rectangular base that projects substantially beyond both sides of the flight; join successive flight ends with exactly two full-width rectangular intermediate landings; offset the flights around a large rectangular well that remains open through the middle of the structure; terminate the upper flight at a broad rectangular top landing aligned over the base to create a tall rectilinear silhouette
examples.checklist_item: Are the flights offset around a large rectangular well that remains open through the middle of the structure?
examples.verifier_evidence: Compared with the original’s circular spiral around a solid central column, the modified top view shows straight flights offset along opposite sides of a large, clearly empty rectangular central area.
examples.category_source: assigned in this harvest from the v160 definitions (provisional; not human-coded)
examples.explanation: From the top, the switch-back flights cover a solid rectangle with no open well; Sol reported "a large, clearly empty rectangular central area".
examples.explanation_source: harvest observation of the renders (annotator recorded no rationale)

examples.instruction: Keep the modified result identifiable and visually coherent as a version of the source object while applying the requested edits; Reconstruct the staircase as a broad annular helix surrounding a large open cylindrical shaft instead of a solid central spine; replace the solid disk base with an annular ring base aligned beneath the inner and outer edges of the helical flight; add exactly three thick outer columns spaced around the ring and extending from the base to the upper landing; form the upper landing as a complete annular ring aligned directly above the ring base; keep the cylindrical central opening broad and continuous through the base ring, helical treads, and upper landing ring
examples.checklist_item: Is the staircase a broad annular helix surrounding a large open cylindrical shaft instead of a solid central spine?
examples.verifier_evidence: The modified top view shows only a small central opening relative to the staircase’s overall diameter, not a large open cylindrical shaft surrounded by a broad annular helix.
examples.category_source: assigned in this harvest from the v160 definitions (provisional; not human-coded)
examples.explanation: The side views show the central column removed so the helix wraps an open shaft; Sol judged from the top view, where the top landing hides most of the shaft, and failed the item.
examples.explanation_source: harvest observation of the renders (annotator recorded no rationale)

categories.name: Compositional completeness
categories.definition: Checking all / every / both / exactly quantifiers and multi-attribute conjunctions instead of passing on partial satisfaction.

examples.instruction: Keep the modified result identifiable and visually coherent as a version of the source object while applying the requested edits; Rearrange the treads in the lower two revolutions into a clear alternating long-short radial rhythm; make every tread in the lower two revolutions approximately twice as thick as its original counterpart; reshape every tread in the upper two revolutions with a pronounced pointed outer tip; increase the radial reach of every tread in the upper two revolutions by about 40 percent
examples.checklist_item: Does every tread in the upper two revolutions have a pronounced pointed outer tip?
examples.verifier_evidence: In the modified right view, multiple clearly visible treads across the upper two revolutions terminate in flat, squared-off outer ends rather than pronounced points; the original counterparts are likewise blunt.
examples.label_source: v160_codex_review (image re-check by Codex in the v160 taxonomy audit; NOT a human label)
examples.v160_rationale: Across the modified front and side views, the upper two revolutions consist of treads with pronounced narrow pointed outer tips.
examples.explanation: "Every tread in the upper two revolutions" does have a pointed tip in the edited views (v160); Sol cited squared-off ends and failed the item.
examples.explanation_source: harvest summary of the v160 rationale + render check

examples.instruction: Keep the underlying original object category broadly recognizable while applying the requested semantic reinterpretation; Reconstruct the bracket into a broad retro-spacecraft silhouette with two swept tapered mounting arms joined by a thick crescent-shaped brace; add a large triangular dorsal fin centered at the inside corner; form three long evenly spaced oval vents through the crescent brace; build one large layered nacelle pod along each mounting arm; split each free end into a broad forked wingtip
examples.checklist_item: Is one large layered nacelle pod built along each mounting arm?
examples.verifier_evidence: The modified bottom view clearly shows one large raised pod centered along each of the two mounting arms, with layered block-like forms absent from the original.
examples.label_source: human_patch_20260917 (main_patch_20260917T012508Z) — label changed in the patch: yes→no
examples.category_source: assigned in this harvest from the v160 definitions (provisional; not human-coded)
examples.explanation: Multi-attribute conjunction: in the bottom view each arm carries a single plain cylinder; the (patched) human label rejects "one large layered nacelle pod", Sol passed on the presence of a pod.
examples.explanation_source: harvest observation of the renders (annotator recorded no rationale)

categories.name: Part–attribute grounding
categories.definition: Binding each attribute to the part the query names, without substituting a neighbouring or newly added part (or the other image).

examples.instruction: Keep the underlying original object category broadly recognizable while applying the requested semantic reinterpretation; Rebuild the sink body with a wide stepped-octagonal Art Deco silhouette formed by three clearly separated tiers; reshape the basin into a deep faceted octagon with two broad descending ledges; reconstruct the faucet as a tall angular inverted-U spout with a wide rectangular profile; add a large raised sunburst panel along the faucet edge behind the spout; add three long parallel speed-line ribs to each exterior side face
examples.checklist_item: Is there a large raised sunburst panel along the faucet edge behind the spout?
examples.verifier_evidence: The original front shows a clearly raised fan-like array of multiple rays, while the modified front panel behind the spout exposes only two parallel vertical bars; no large, visibly distinguishable sunburst is present.
examples.label_source: v160_codex_review (image re-check by Codex in the v160 taxonomy audit; NOT a human label)
examples.v160_rationale: A large raised fan of radial bars is plainly visible behind the spout.
examples.explanation: The edited front view does show a fan of radial bars behind the spout; Sol's evidence attributes the fan to the original and only "two parallel vertical bars" (apparently the uprights of the new inverted-U spout) to the edit — the two images' parts are swapped.
examples.explanation_source: harvest summary of the v160 rationale + render check

supplementary_category.name: Evidence existence (hallucinated evidence)
supplementary_category.definition: Passing an item when the target is missing or the render is empty/fragmentary, describing parts that are not there (exp3 TAXONOMY.md). Outside the 7 v160 categories.

examples.instruction: Keep the modified result identifiable and visually coherent as a version of the source object while applying the requested edits; Rebuild the highest-reaching side arm with a sharp right-angle elbow formed by an outward segment followed by a segment parallel to the main trunk; make this side arm approximately twice its original thickness; extend its tip to the same height as the main trunk crown
examples.checklist_item: Does its tip reach the same height as the main trunk crown?
examples.verifier_evidence: In the modified front view, the rebuilt side arm’s parallel upright segment terminates level with the main trunk crown, unlike the visibly lower original arm tip.
examples.category_source: not one of the 7 v160 categories; matches the exp3 casebook category evidence_existence (harvest assignment)
examples.explanation: All six edited renders are empty background (no foreground pixels; harvest check), yet Sol medium answered yes with a specific description of the arm tip. All three Sol high votes were no.
examples.explanation_source: harvest observation of the renders (annotator recorded no rationale)

examples.instruction: Keep the modified result identifiable and visually coherent as a version of the source object while applying the requested edits; Rebuild the lower trunk and two opposing side arms as a broad arch-shaped crown supported by two tall outer uprights; curve the two outer uprights inward above the shortened central trunk so their tips nearly meet with a narrow gap; create one large rounded opening framed by the outer arms and positioned entirely above the central trunk tip; make the two outer uprights reach the same height and stand conspicuously taller than the central trunk; flare both arm-to-trunk transitions into broad sweeping curves that widen the lower half of the arch
examples.checklist_item: Are the two outer uprights approximately equal in height and conspicuously taller than the central trunk?
examples.verifier_evidence: In the modified front view, the two opposing outer uprights have top tips at approximately the same level, and both extend conspicuously higher than the top of the shortened central trunk; the original front view shows the side arms ending much lower than the tall central trunk.
examples.category_source: exp3 casebook category evidence_existence (not one of the 7 v160 categories)
examples.explanation: The edit left only scattered fragments (two small arcs and a broken outline); Sol described "two opposing outer uprights" taller than a "shortened central trunk".
